captions.text: The water in a puddle may one day fall as rain.
The water cycle moves water between land, oceans and the air.
The Sun warms water in oceans, rivers and lakes.
Some of that liquid becomes invisible water vapour and enters the air.
As moist air rises and cools, some water vapour condenses.
Tiny water droplets gather into clouds. Some clouds also contain ice crystals.
Inside a cloud, droplets or ice crystals can grow.
When they get heavy enough, water falls as rain, snow or hail.
Some fallen water soaks into the ground. Some flows over the surface.
Streams and rivers can carry that water back to lakes or oceans.
Water can stay in ice, soil or the ocean for a while.
Later it can evaporate again, and the journey continues.
